screenshots.shows: Hero collage, angled and overlapping: panels from Innovation, Azul and Crew strewn over the help page. Its job is to show that the extension covers many surfaces across several games — breadth, not any particular control. Not read for individual elements

steps: Build the working tree with `npm run build` and load it unpacked, so the shot matches the tree rather than the store release
Open the side panel across a live Innovation, Azul and Crew table and shoot enough panels to read as a spread
Compose them at angles over the help page, matching the existing frame's arrangement
Judge the result by whether it still reads as broad coverage, not by whether any panel in it is current

steps: Help page eye menu, "Compact BGA header"
Frame the header region down to the top of the board, with the option off, then on

screenshots.shows: The folded top bar under the amber hazard stripes, lit by an opponent's Clock demanding back the cards the viewer revealed. That is the one state which raises them: a reaction owed during another player's turn

steps: Innovation table, eye menu, "Police-line highlight" on
Wait for a reaction owed on an opponent's turn (a dogma demand, or a share you may take). It cannot be staged, so catch it when a real table offers one
Frame the bar alone, cropping away the page above, below and to either side of it
Stamp the hairline with `python docs/screenshots/capture/lib/border.py`, since the bar's own amber has no edge against a light page

screenshots.shows: Nucleum turn history rendered into BGA's own log column, with the lightbulb view switch, per-player row colours, the viewer's rows tinted, and "more..." at the foot. Background keyed out to transparency, so it composites on a light or dark page

steps: Enable "Show in BGA game log" and open a live Nucleum table
Pick a window containing a railway that completed a link and a turn with a repeated action
Capture BGA's log column including the lightbulb and the "more..." control

Key BGA's wood out afterwards: the panels are rounded rectangles, so mask them by geometry (not by colour — the fill and the wood differ by ~28 levels of blue alone), inset one pixel past the antialiased band, and stroke the outline rather than the canvas

screenshots.shows: Nucleum's player panels, BGA's own and then folded — three panels in 706 pixels of column and then 368, the beginner notice dropped and the first player marked by a corner wedge. Background keyed out to transparency, so the gaps between panels show the page

steps: Nucleum table, its display menu, "Compact player panels"
Frame the player panel column with the option off, then on
A table including a player on their first game shows the dropped notice
Trim the near-white page margin on the right before anything else

Key BGA's wood out afterwards: the panels are rounded rectangles, so mask them by geometry (not by colour — the fill and the wood differ by ~28 levels of blue alone), inset one pixel past the antialiased band, and stroke the outline rather than the canvas
